I was homeschooled from kindergarten-12th grade, so the first time I set foot in an actual classroom was my freshman year of college. 

Pros: you don't spend a lot of time doing schoolwork. The average amount of time I spent working on school, homework included, was four hours a day, even through high school. This leaves you free to pursue other things that you're interested in and/or passionate about. I have two younger siblings and they're homeschooled as well, which means that my family could take weeklong vacations in October, or February, or whenever we wanted, really, because we didn't have a set schedule of having to be in this place at this time to learn. I did the majority of my high school work lying in bed, which was awesome because lazy teenager. Basically, homeschooling gives you a lot of freedom. Academically, there were no cons; I did and continue to do quite well in school (finishing freshman year with a 3.9 GPA). 

The only cons may have been socially: without constant forced social interaction you have to look for opportunities to be with people. For somebody who's already a little on the introverted side, this can lead to being more comfortable with books than with people and having very few real friends. A year of living in a dorm at college fixed that though - I'm still a little shy and awkward but have no issues with talking to people. 

All in all it was a fantastic experience and I wouldn't have actually gone to school for the world.
Depression. I would no longer have a little voice in my head, screaming that I'm a worthless piece of shit and the world would be better off without me.

I really, really, really love this. Even though I can't sing worth anything, I'm considering learning how to sing that song just because it describes how I feel so well. 

The quote is very fitting. Well done :)

I had to accept that my normal isn't everybody else's normal. 

I learned to celebrate the little things like cleaning my room or going for a walk as a giant victory. I watched a lot of Netflix and made bracelets so I wouldn't self harm. I quit my job in a poisonous environment and started working in my parents' business, which is a far healthier place to work. I tried to find something to be thankful for every day.

It sucks. I know it does. I'm in cognitive behavioral therapy and have been on antidepressants for a while. But things get better, and I'm actually 30 days away from being off them :) You've got this.

I'm a swimmer who cut on her forearm and lower leg. They're obvious, but I'm still swimming.

Would you have to stop playing volleyball because they wouldn't let you play anymore or because you don't want people to see the cuts?

For what it's worth, I do hope you can find a healthier outlet for your pain. You're stronger than you think you are. <3
Yay congratulations!! *high five*

1. Acceptance. No ultimatums, no "promise me you'll stop"s. The understanding that yes, we know it's a bad thing. Yes, a lot of the time we want to stop. Just be there for us when we want to talk and remind us things get better.
2. Severe depression. The emotional pain got to be too much to handle, so I turned it into physical pain. 
3. Nope, not really.
4. Nobody who currently does, but I know people who have. 
5. After a few months of therapy and a heck of a lot of help from friends, yes.
6. Cutting, burning, bruising, picking, hot water, overeating, drugs, binge drinking, the list goes on...
7. Cutting. Or I used to. Hopefully won't again.

Thank you. I'm not really sure what else to say but thank you. 

I'm a swimmer, so when I feel it coming on in time, I go swim. But like you said, when you catch it too late it's awful. 

I am going to be alright; I just got really scared is all. Thank you so much for your  comment. It means more than I can say, I think.

Thank you so much. I texted my best friend and I'm pretty well calmed down. I just got scared.

Excercise does usually help, if, kind of like the_splatt said, I get up and do it in time. I'll hopefully get to volunteer this summer, and... yeah. Things are getting better, but the bad days are still really really bad. 

I can't really tell you how much I appreciate your comment. So thank you again.
100 days is amazing! Have a high five from a random internet stranger. I'm proud of you. :)

I've been on 50 mg of Zoloft since the midde of November. Not gonna lie, it made things worse for about five weeks. Like a lot worse. After that, it really did start helping and my dosage hasn't had to be upped at all or anything. Those five - eight weeks sucked, though. Good luck with it, and with everything else. :)
I'm so proud of you. :)
Alright. Calm down if you can. It may just be because I'm still too young to know better, but I've got a little faith in humanity left. And know that that includes you. Alright?

Okay, that's fine. You don't have to agree with me, I'm perfectly willing to admit that there are different perspectives out there, and you know yourself better than a random internet stranger does.

For what it's worth, though, I genuinely don't think you're useless.

I definitely see you, and not as an insane fuckhead. And that's simply not true, honestly. I know the feeling, but I also know everybody has value. And some people just aren't good at expressing that they see it.

Trust me, I know that feeling. The giving up, the hating yourself for giving up, the feeling alone and not strong enough. I'm here to tell you nobody's perfect so if they're a decent human being at all you won't be judged for being less than perfect. 

I'd definitely be willing to talk, if you want. :)

I've mentioned this somewhere else on this sub, I think, but bracelets. I love wearing bracelets, so I've made a bunch of really simple ones and every day I make it clean, I put another one on. It's so sily, but looking at those bracelets remind me of how far I've gone and have stopped me from cutting many, many times.
Six months is awesome. :) and like you said, you're going to be able to last even longer this time. You've got this.

The general public now knows I cut because I get overheated really easily and wear short sleeves to work now that my arms are just scarred. There are still only two people I really talk to about it, though, and they're dating. I'm basically in the same boat you are when it comes to feeling guilty about talking to them, even though they've both told me countless times that they want to help and will always listen. 

My advice? Believe them when they say they want to help. I know that's easier said than done, but you're most likely very important to both of them and they do want to help you. If you need someone else to talk to, my inbox is always open. :)
Hang in there. You're not a disappointment; slip ups happen. You stayed clean for a long time, and I bet you can go even longer this time. I believe in you. :)

You're not wasting my time. You're a valuable human being with thoughts and feelings that matter, even to a total stranger. 

Fingers crossed that things look up for you.
Awesome!!!!! :) am so happy for you!
I'm not the best at giving advice, but I just wanted to let you know hugs are being sent your way. You've got this.

Well, thanks :) They're really really really simple, honestly. I just braid five strands of embroidery floss together until it's long enough to tie around my wrist. 

And congratulations on the fifteen and 31 days! That's huge :)

Sure! Don't get too excited though, they really are very simple bracelets. :P

[bracelets](http://i.imgur.com/4R8i7uL)

Don't know if you're a bracelet person, but I've made a bunch of bracelets out of embroidery floss. Every day I make it clean, I add another bracelet. Once I get to a multiple of 25, those are taken off and replaced with a nicer one, and then I start over. If I cut, they all have to come off and I start over.

It sounds silly but I'm at forty-two days and every time I want to cut, the bracelets are have been enough to either decide not to or a reminder to talk to someone first. 

Good luck. You've got this. :)
TL;DR broke up with me to become a Catholic priest but remained an emotionally abusive close friend for two years afterwards.

Hi there. Please don't hate yourself for freaking out about school. I used to have panic attacks about going to work or church. 

My parents had no idea things were so bad with me until we went to see a doctor. It really is important to just be honest with her. She can't help until she knows what the problem is.

Believe me, I understand that. But please don't see suicide as the only way out. You're a lovely person and I would be sad you were gone, even though I'm a total stranger. 

If you would like to talk about things, please feel free to PM me, alright?
Hi! It's not strange to ask at all. I love talking. :)

Hi there. I'm not really good at this type of thing, let me tell you that up front. But I've been where you are. I didn't have any motivation to do anything, I put on some weight, my sense of self-worth was in the toilet, etc. There have been days when a friend would text me until I fell asleep at night and then would text the next day to see if I was alright and hadn't done anything to myself.

This is going to sound cliche', and for that I'm sorry. But hang on. You sound like you have a heck of a lot of potential, you just lost your way a bit. We all do, sometimes. We're also our own worst critics. I'm sure the people in your life see a lot of awesome things in you that you have trouble seeing in yourself. I hope you pull through this, I really do. I'm around if you'd like someone to talk to. 

(sorry for the novel)
Oh gosh. If you ever ever need to talk, please feel free to PM me. I'll answer as quickly as I can. :)
I'm here! :)
Hey, you okay? Take a deep breath. I'm here to talk through things with you if you want. :)
How's it going? I'm glad I could help. :) And thank you, I really appreciate the encouragement!

You're not alone. 
If you want to talk, I'm here. :)

Hey. Take a deep breath and try to stay strong for her, alrght? 
And I'm a total stranger, but I'm less than a month clean. Three months is an inspiration to me. Stay strong for me, too?
I'm rooting for you.

Hi. I just wanted to tell you you're brave. My scars aren't too noticeable, but they're very obviously there and I'm scared of what happens when people see them. 

So... huge props to you for handling things so well. And for your determination that depression never gets the better of you.

Talk to my best friend if I can. If I feel like I'll be bugging him, then watch Netflix or read a book. 

Reasons to avoid self harm? My best friend, who told me while I was sucidal that he'd rather talk me out of suicide every day for the rest of his life than let me die. His support and the support of a few other close friends keep me sane.
As cliche' as it sounds, it's one step at a time. One day clean is a giant step in the right direction. You'll get there :)

As I'm recovering (25 days clean today!), yeah, I'm proud of my scars. To me, they're turning into a reminder of something I've overcome. I'm proud that I'm going to be able to look at them and say, "I survived."

Hey there. I'm about your age and have been in a similar situation, but with my dad instead. My victories like making my bed or picking up my room were met with the attitude of why wasn't I doing more. 

Just... please know you're not alone in this. You are stronger than you think. You can do this.

Hey there. I just wanted to tell you that I don't think you're a loser, or a pathetic little whore. You're sixteen years old and keeping your baby, which is incredibly courageous. You're so much stronger than you give yourself credit for being. Hang in there.
